_comment: Recorded result of the OWASP CRS regression suite against prx-waf.
This file is the CI gate. `tests/ftw/run.sh` with BASELINE set exits
non-zero when a paranoia level produces MORE failures than the number
below plus `tolerance`. It is deliberately a data file and not a constant
inside the workflow: moving the number has to be a reviewable diff in the
pull request that earned it.
Improving the number is not an error, but the run prints a reminder to
lower the baseline in the same PR — otherwise the ratchet stops working.
KEYED BY MODE FIRST, because the two modes ask the WAF different questions
and their failure counts are not comparable:
log    The corpus as written. WAF in DetectionOnly (`log_only_mode`), and
go-ftw judges each test by the rule ids prx-waf wrote to its audit
log between that stage's two X-CRS-Test markers. This is the
posture ModSecurity v2 + CRS (100%) and Coraza (100%) are measured
in, so the log column is the one that belongs next to theirs.
cloud  WAF enforcing, verdicts from HTTP status codes, with the corpus's
log assertions restated as 403/200 by gen_overrides.py. Measures
the blocking decision a user experiences. Strictly noisier as a
detection measurement in BOTH directions: a negative test can only
say 'nothing blocked' (so an unrelated rule fails it — 290 of the
PL4 over-blocks), and a positive test passes on any 403 at all (so
a rule that never fired still scores). Both halves grew when the
response phase landed, because the tests it now covers are counted.
Numbers are only comparable at the same crs_version, the same go_ftw
version, the same mode and the same paranoia level. Restate all four
whenever the figure is quoted anywhere.
Both modes count the five `retry_once` tests (959100-1/-3, 980170-1/-2/-3)
in the denominator. go-ftw aborts the entire run when one of them fails
twice (runner/run.go, RunTest), so run.sh quarantines them out of the bulk
run and re-runs each on its own; classify.py merges the individual verdicts
back in. Nothing is dropped and nothing is force-passed.
RESPONSE PHASE. The CRS 950–956 rules are evaluated as of this recording,
which is where the log-mode gain over the previous baseline (2671 / 3618 /
4093 at c3eb2dd) comes from: +68 / +78 / +78 at PL1 / PL2 / PL4, every one of
them a response-phase test. Cloud mode is unchanged (+0) BY CONSTRUCTION and
not by accident: response inspection defaults to observe
(PRXWAF_RESPONSE_INSPECT_MODE), so a leaking response is logged and then
delivered, and the status code cloud mode reads stays 200. Re-running cloud
PL4 with PRXWAF_RESPONSE_INSPECT_MODE=enforce scores 4020 (86.01%), +27 with
zero tests lost — noted here rather than recorded as the baseline, because
the default posture is what CI has to gate on.
The bucket split moved for a second reason: classify.py no longer files every
response-phase failure under not-implemented ('the engine never feeds it a
response body'), because it now does. Response-phase failures are ordinary
missed detections / over-blocks / paranoia-scope exclusions and are counted
as such. Only the buckets are affected; passed and failed are not.

log._comment: go-ftw default mode; verdicts from the rule ids in prx-waf's audit log, WAF in DetectionOnly.

cloud._comment: Verdicts from HTTP status codes, WAF enforcing, gen_overrides.py supplying the missing status expectations.
